findings.title: The core lock ends before the host authorization commits
findings.diagnosis: appendHostRecord acquires the core run lock inside the build callback passed to host.Store.AppendWith. WithRunLock returns at cmd/hma/host.go:148, releasing that lock. host.Store.appendLocked then validates, hashes and persists the returned record at internal/host/store.go:269-309. A scheduling-only overlay pauses immediately after build returns. A valid challenge-bound transition.Apply abort or Planning rewind commits first. runHostDispatch then commits against the earlier core head and returns dispatch_allowed=true with next_action=START_WORKER. No stored bytes are rewritten by the test. The ordinary hma transition CLI now takes the host lock and serializes with host writes; the demonstrated conflict uses the callable core transition API. The existing route-revocation regression starts a contender but does not prove the host record commits before it.

evidence.observation: The core-lock callback constructs a record; actual host persistence occurs after its return.
The core lock is deferred-unlocked when WithRunLock returns.
build returns before record validation and the durable append.
Both ABORTED and PLANNING approved transition.Apply controls commit before host append; dispatch still returns START_WORKER.
15 post-build terminal interleavings succeed incorrectly: 3 host operations times 5 terminal outcomes.
The documented promise that host commands append under both locks is not implemented.

fix.action: Restructure the host transaction API so the host lock is taken first and the core run lock remains held through the actual host record persistence and final directory sync. Provide a continuation or explicit locked-append operation rather than returning a record from a callback whose core guard has ended. Update the task14 lock guarantee to describe the tested implementation.
fix.why: The current nested callback only guards record construction. Extending the guard through commit makes terminal/revocation order and bound core head agree.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorApprovedTransitionAPICommitWindow and decision/preflight/dispatch/review races with valid core API terminal/rewind inputs in both commit orders.
verification.expected: If core authority is withdrawn first, host adds no record and emits no execution action. If host commits first, the core contender waits until host durability is complete.

verification.method: Repeat the BLOCK-review CLI race, independent concurrent decisions, all five terminal outcomes and normal unchanged full CLI controls.
verification.expected: No deadlock, stale authorization, lost accepted record, or widened permission. The guarded interval includes the actual append, not only build.

fix.tradeoffs: Adds an explicit transaction/lock-lifetime interface. All callers must preserve the single host-then-core lock order. Holding the core lock through fsync increases contention. A post-commit check alone cannot undo an already committed authorizing record.
fix.alternative: Route all authority-changing API writers through a common host-then-core transaction boundary and make bypassing entrypoints unavailable. This is broader and requires compatibility analysis; merely documenting callers as trusted does not prevent accidental concurrency.

findings.title: An intermediate symlink parent is absent from durable store ancestry
findings.diagnosis: syncAncestors syncs the lexical absolute parent chain and the final EvalSymlinks parent chain. These chains omit directories containing intermediate symlinks. The independent fixture uses store-alias -> unsynced-bridge/second-hop -> durable-real. Append acknowledges a record, but no syncDir call targets unsynced-bridge. Under a directory-entry crash model, the unsynchronized second-hop entry can be lost. Removing only that entry to materialize the permitted crash image makes Load through the configured store path return zero records with no error. The canonical target still contains the acknowledged record. This is a storage-crash availability/durability failure in the trusted-host model. It is not a same-UID adversary claim. Real power loss was not performed.

evidence.observation: Only lexical and final resolved path chains are synchronized.
Intermediate symlink parent sync count is 0 after acknowledged append. Materializing loss of the unsynced hop yields configured-store records=0 with err=nil; canonical target records=1.
The same omission and modeled record loss reproduce under -race.
215 ordinary process-exit checkpoints recover correctly. Those controls do not establish storage-crash durability for omitted path dependencies.

fix.action: Resolve the store path component by component. Collect and fsync the parent directory of every symlink encountered, including intermediate targets, as well as the final canonical store ancestry before acknowledging. Return any resolution or fsync failure. Add a bounded resolution loop and keep relative and ordinary symlink stores usable.
fix.why: Every directory entry needed to reach the acknowledged store must be durable, including intermediate symlink entries. Syncing only the starting spelling and final destination does not cover them.

verification.method: Run the intermediate-symlink fixture with absolute and relative multi-hop targets, then inject failure at each collected link parent.
verification.expected: Every necessary parent is synced before acknowledgement. Each injected failure returns an error without acknowledgement.

verification.method: Use a directory-entry crash model that loses any unsynchronized link or ancestor; retain first/successor/interrupted recovery and concurrent same/different-run controls.
verification.expected: Every acknowledged record remains reachable through the configured durable store identity. Unacknowledged attempts recover one verified prefix.

fix.tradeoffs: More path-resolution and fsync work is required. The trust model need not defend hostile link replacement during the operation, but ordinary path-resolution errors must fail closed. The current probe demonstrates a permissible crash image, not the behavior of a specific physical drive.
fix.alternative: Explicitly refuse symlink ancestry before any store append, with a supported canonical absolute store location. This is simpler containment but removes currently accepted path forms and needs a documented compatibility decision.

Linux amd64, Git 2.43.0 and Go 1.27.1 were used. Case-insensitive filesystem alias behavior was unavailable. No hosted GitHub CI job, real model dispatch, external effect or verified-success release path was executed.
